findings.description: Import deletes the pending file without locking it against concurrent writers.
findings.failure_mode: After import reads the pending ledger, a worker can successfully append another decision to that file. Import commits only its earlier snapshot and then removes the entire pending file, permanently deleting the worker's newly appended decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinate imports and pending writes with the same source-file lock, held from the pending snapshot through removal. Ensure this locking also works across checkouts.

findings.description: The ledger is committed before fallible reference rewrites, but imports have no durable retry mapping.
findings.failure_mode: If mktemp or a rewrite fails, the command exits after importing the rows while leaving the pending file intact. Retrying allocates fresh DEC ids and imports duplicate decisions. References already rewritten during the first attempt retain the first ids, while subsequent rewrites use the second ids.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist the PEND-to-DEC mapping transactionally with the import and reuse it on retries. Stage and validate rewrite outputs before committing, and make recovery resume the existing import.

findings.description: Rejecting a proposed replacement leaves its predecessor's supersede_proposed_by pointing to the rejected row.
findings.failure_mode: An agent proposes a replacement for a decided row, then that replacement is rejected. Every subsequent agent supersede attempt against the original row fails with 'a replacement is already proposed', because op_supersede checks only whether the stale pointer is populated. The normal proposal workflow cannot recover.
findings.suggested_fix: When rejecting a replacement, atomically clear the predecessor's supersede_proposed_by if it points to that replacement, and include both rows in verification.

findings.description: live_run_signal() is `ctx_signals | grep -q '^live '` and the script runs with `set -euo pipefail`. grep -q exits on the first matching line. ctx_signals keeps emitting lines afterwards (it forks jq between echoes, so the timing gap is milliseconds), and its next echo hits a closed pipe: the left-hand subshell is killed by SIGPIPE (status 141). Under pipefail the pipeline status is 141, so `if live_run_signal; then die ...` in op_confirm (line 509) evaluates FALSE whenever two or more signal lines exist (e.g. a fresh .run/unattended.json plus a RUNNING state.json, or any live line followed by the `prd prd-status` line). That is precisely the autonomous-run shape the guard exists for: autonomous-agent/SKILL.md now tells runs to write the marker while run state is RUNNING.
findings.failure_mode: confirm is accepted during a live unattended run, moving agent-proposed rows to `decided` from within the run; the documented refusal (decisions.md rule 5) silently does not fire. The same pattern would also break any future `if ctx_signals | grep -q` caller.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture first, then test: `live_run_signal(){ local s; s="$(ctx_signals)" || true; grep -q '^live ' <<< "$s"; }` (or `[[ "$(ctx_signals)" == *$'\n'"live "* || "$(ctx_signals)" == "live "* ]]`). Add a bats case with two live signals (marker + RUNNING state) asserting confirm is refused.

findings.description: The only thing that makes confirm, reject-on-decided, supersede-as-operator and `context --clear` 'operator-only' is `[[ "$(o recorded-by)" == decisions-command ]]`, i.e. a caller-supplied string. decisions.md and the file header assert that an agent cannot confirm its own decisions, but any session with Bash can run `dec-write-lib.sh confirm --id DEC-0007 --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:... --answer-ref cli:...` and the row records `decided_by: operator`. `disable-model-invocation` only blocks the Skill tool from starting /decisions, and the bats grep only covers checked-in command/skill text, not runtime calls.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or a prompt-injected session) self-confirms proposed rows with operator attribution; the ledger's core provenance claim (`decided` only by the operator) is not enforced by the writer.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind the operator path to something the model cannot fabricate from text: e.g. have /decisions write a short-lived nonce file under .run that the lib checks and consumes, and/or make confirm refuse whenever `is_unattended` (not only `live_run_signal`). At minimum, document in the header and decisions.md that the gate is advisory, not a security boundary.

findings.description: In worktree/--pending mode resolve_target creates decisions-pending.yaml with `cat > "$TARGET" <<EOF` when the file is absent. This happens before acquire_lock. Two concurrent `new` calls in the same worktree (e.g. parallel subagents) can both observe `! -f`, writer A then locks, appends, swaps; writer B's deferred `cat >` then truncates the file back to `decisions: []` before B locks and appends its own row.
findings.failure_mode: A's PEND row is silently lost from the pending file; the bead that references its PEND id dangles at import time.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the bootstrap inside the lock (acquire_lock first, then create if still absent), or create atomically with `set -o noclobber` / write to a temp and `ln` it into place, falling through if the file now exists.

findings.description: op_import swaps the live ledger (verify_and_swap) and only afterwards runs the --rewrite loop and `rm -f -- "$from"`. The rewrite loop uses `mktemp "${p}.XXXXXX"` and `mv -f` without `|| warn`, so under `set -e` an unwritable target directory or a read-only file aborts the script after the ledger has already been changed, leaving the pending file in place. Nothing in import dedupes against rows already imported (it validates ids only as PEND-<hex> and appends).
findings.failure_mode: Re-running import after a partial failure appends the same rows again under fresh DEC ids; since the ledger is append-only each duplicate must be rejected by hand, and beads rewritten in the first pass now point at the first copy while the printed map points at the second.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove/rename the pending file (e.g. to .imported) immediately after verify_and_swap succeeds, before rewrites; make each rewrite failure a warn-and-continue; optionally refuse import when a live row already carries a transition/recorded_by identical to a pending row.

findings.description: An agent supersede sets `supersede_proposed_by = <new id>` on the decided row and lands the replacement as `proposed`. If the operator rejects that proposed replacement, op_reject touches only the rejected row; the decided row keeps `supersede_proposed_by`. op_supersede's non-operator path (line 600-601) then dies with 'a replacement is already proposed for DEC-xxxx' forever, and op_confirm's superseded hop can never fire again for that row.
findings.failure_mode: After one rejected proposal, no agent/flatline/dissent voice can ever propose superseding that decision again; only the operator path (which skips the check) can, which contradicts the lifecycle described in the header and decisions.md.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_reject, when the rejected row has `.supersedes`, load that row and clear `supersede_proposed_by` if it equals the rejected id (add it to the touched list for verify_and_swap). Add a bats case: supersede (agent) -> reject -> supersede (agent) succeeds.
